title: Word counts in a StringMap
hints: The starter throws away every map that `StringMap.add` returns, so `m` stays empty. A map never changes, so you have to keep the new one.
Use `List.fold_left`: the accumulator is the map so far, starting at `StringMap.empty`.
`List.fold_left (fun m w -> let n = match StringMap.find_opt w m with Some n -> n | None -> 0 in StringMap.add w (n + 1) m) StringMap.empty words`.

answer.code:
module StringMap = Map.Make (String)

let count_words (words : string list) : int StringMap.t =
  List.fold_left
    (fun m w ->
      let n = match StringMap.find_opt w m with Some n -> n | None -> 0 in
      StringMap.add w (n + 1) m)
    StringMap.empty words
answer.explain: The reference folds over the words with the map as the accumulator. Each step looks up the old count with `find_opt` and returns `StringMap.add w (n + 1) m`, a new map, which the fold hands to the next step. `StringMap.bindings` lists the keys in sorted order, so no sort is needed.
